title: Standings double-count seasons present in both Brasileirão sources
evidence: query.ex:74-75 standings/3 filters competition via exact_or_contains? (query.ex:119-122, a substring match). search_key("Brasileirão Historical")="brasileirao historical" contains search_key("Brasileirão")="brasileirao", so the default competition matches BOTH Brasileirao_Matches.csv ("Brasileirão") and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv ("Brasileirão Historical", catalog.ex:10). Verified: both CSVs hold 380 rows for 2019 and each independently gives Flamengo 90pts/38 games; team_key strips the "-RJ" suffix (catalog.ex:200-205) so the two rows merge -> Flamengo ~180pts/76 games. _factual.json score 0.0.
suggestion: Match competition exactly (or map each source to a canonical competition id) and/or deduplicate overlapping match sources so a season is aggregated once.

title: MCP tool inputSchema omits properties/required
evidence: mcp.ex:14-19 tool/2 returns inputSchema %{"type"=>"object","additionalProperties"=>true} with no "properties"/"required" for all 7 tools; e.g. standings does required(arguments,"season") (Map.fetch! at mcp.ex:130) yet advertises no season arg. Valid JSON Schema and callable, but clients/LLMs cannot discover argument names/types from tools/list.
suggestion: Populate inputSchema.properties + required per tool (season, team, team_a/team_b, competition, name/nationality/club) so agents can call tools without guessing.

title: Standings test does not exercise the multi-source real-data path
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_test.exs:62-68 asserts standings only on an in-memory catalog whose matches are all competition "Brasileirão" (no "Brasileirão Historical" rows), so the double-counting on the shipped dataset is never caught; test_coverage=1.0 (scores.json) reflects this clean path only.
suggestion: Add a standings test over the loaded Kaggle catalog (or a fixture containing both a Brasileirão and a Brasileirão Historical row for one season) asserting a single, correctly-aggregated table.
